headline: Microorganisms are everywhere—trillions live on and inside you right now
universal_truth: Scale changes everything; most of life exists at sizes we can't see
fun_facts: Your body contains about 38 trillion bacteria—slightly more than your human cells
A single teaspoon of soil contains billions of microorganisms
Most microbes are harmless or helpful; only a tiny fraction cause disease
discussion_questions: How does knowing you host trillions of microbes change how you see yourself?
Why are most microbes helpful rather than harmful?
What would happen if all microbes suddenly disappeared?

hook.script: You're never alone. Right now, trillions of microorganisms live on your skin, in your gut, in your mouth. You host more bacterial cells than human cells. Most of these tiny hitchhikers aren't invaders—they're partners.

cliff.script: We think of microbes as germs—things that make us sick. But most microbes are harmless or beneficial. What are all these trillions of tiny creatures actually doing?
cliff.prompt: What do the microbes in your body actually do?

options.text: They help digest food, train the immune system, produce vitamins, and protect against harmful invaders
options.response: Yes. Your microbiome is a partner system. Gut bacteria help digest fiber, produce vitamin K, and crowd out pathogens. You're a collaboration, not just an individual.

options.text: Most are dormant and don't affect us much
options.response: They're actually very active—many are essential for digestion and health...

fact1.title: Microbial Majority
fact1.script: Your body hosts about 38 trillion bacteria—slightly outnumbering your 30 trillion human cells. By cell count, you're barely half human. Add viruses and fungi, and you're a walking ecosystem, not just an organism.

fact2.title: Essential Partners
fact2.script: Gut bacteria break down fiber you can't digest, produce vitamins you need, and train your immune system. Without them, you'd be malnourished and vulnerable to infection. They're not passengers—they're essential crew.

fact3.title: Soil Abundance
fact3.script: A teaspoon of healthy soil contains billions of microorganisms—more than all humans on Earth. They decompose dead matter, fix nitrogen, and enable plant growth. Life on land depends on soil microbes. They're the hidden foundation.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Scale changes everything. Most of life exists at sizes we can't see. The invisible majority—microbes—make the visible world possible. What we overlook may be what matters most.

outro.script: That's Day 149. Tomorrow, we'll explore things that are 'not quite alive'—viruses. Until then, appreciate your microbial partners—trillions of tiny lives working to keep you healthy.

growTrack.title: Invisible Appreciation - Honor What You Can't See
growTrack.activity: Your microbiome works constantly—digesting, protecting, producing. What other invisible systems do you depend on daily? Infrastructure, relationships, processes that run unseen? The invisible often matters more than the visible.
